mainTopic: Deriving from the פסוקים that every main עבודה of a חטאת must be done לשמה, both for its offering type and for its owner, and that doing it otherwise disqualifies it (לעכב)
overview: The גמרא is looking for פסוקים that show a חטאת must be brought לשמה, both for the right type of קרבן (שינוי קודש) and for the right owner (שינוי בעלים). It also wants to show that doing it otherwise disqualifies the חטאת (לעכב), and is not just the ideal way (למצוה). First it finds sources for קבלה and זריקה, and the word 'מחטאתו' makes the owner rule לעכב for the זריקה. רבי יונה and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע then try to extend this to every עבודה from the חטאת of a נזיר. רבינא challenges that proof, and the גמרא adds that a נזיר's חטאת and an ordinary חטאת are too different to learn from each other. רבא tries the חטאת of a מצורע instead, but it runs into the same problem. The idea that two kinds of חטאת can teach the third also fails, because each kind has its own special feature. In the end, a היקש of חטאת to שלמים teaches the מצוה, and the separate פסוקים for each kind of חטאת teach that it is לעכב. The amud closes as the גמרא starts checking which kinds of חטאת have their own פסוק, beginning with חטאת חלב.

steps.title: Collecting the blood must be for the sake of a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'and the כהן shall take of the blood of the חטאת' teaches that קבלה must be done לשם חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering': this teaches that collecting the blood must be done for the sake of a sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list of sources and shows that collecting the blood (קבלה) must be done for the sake of a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for שחיטה was given just before this. The פסוק about taking the blood is said with the word 'חטאת', so the taking has to be done with the thought that this is a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Collecting the animal's blood in a holy vessel
For the sake of (with the intent of) a sin offering
And the priest shall take

phrases.english: "And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:25

phrases.english: that the collection must be for the sake of a sin offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the derivation begun before this section, where שחיטה לשם חטאת was derived.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קבלה of a חטאת must be done לשם חטאת.

steps.title: Where is the source for sprinkling?
steps.stepSummary: We have sources for שחיטה and קבלה. What is the source that זריקה must also be לשם חטאת?
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for slaughtering and collecting. From where do we know this about sprinkling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the next missing piece: a source that sprinkling the blood (זריקה) must also be for the sake of a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of the main עבודות are covered. The rule should apply to זריקה too, but the גמרא wants a פסוק for it and does not just assume it.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for this)
Sprinkling or throwing the blood on the מזבח
From where do we know it?
Slaughtering the animal

phrases.english: And we have found slaughter and collection;
sprinkling, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 1 and asks about the next עבודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that זריקה must be לשם חטאת.

steps.title: Atonement must be for the sake of a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'וכפר עליו הכהן מחטאתו' teaches that the כפרה, which happens through the sprinkling, must be לשם חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the verse says: 'And the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin offering': the atonement must be for the sake of a sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק about כפרה and shows that the sprinkling must be for the sake of a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זריקה is the act that brings the כפרה. So when the פסוק ties the כפרה to the חטאת, it is really telling us that the זריקה must be done לשם חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: As the verse says
And he shall atone
Atonement, which comes through the sprinkling of the blood

phrases.english: As the verse says:
"And the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:26

phrases.english: that the atonement must be for the sake of a sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא וְכִפֶּר עָלָיו הַכֹּהֵן מֵחַטָּאתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'וכפר... מחטאתו' teaches that the כפרה (זריקה) must be לשם חטאת.
steps.whatToRemember: All the main עבודות of a חטאת (שחיטה, קבלה, זריקה) must be done for the sake of a חטאת.

steps.title: Where is the source for the owner?
steps.stepSummary: The sources so far cover a change of offering type (שינוי קודש). What is the source for a change of owner (שינוי בעלים)?
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for changing the type of offering. From where do we know the rule for changing the owner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a second kind of wrong intent: doing the עבודה for a different person instead of the real owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every source so far was about thinking of the animal as a different kind of קרבן. Thinking of it as belonging to someone else is a separate problem, so it needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: Changing the type of offering in one's intent (for example, thinking of it as a שלמים)
Changing the owner in one's intent (doing it for someone else)

phrases.english: We have found a change of the offering type;
a change of owner, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן שִׁנּוּי קֹדֶשׁ, שִׁנּוּי בְּעָלִים מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the type of offering to the owner of the offering.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that the עבודה must be done for the real owner.

steps.title: For him and not for another
steps.stepSummary: The word 'עליו' in the same פסוק teaches that the כפרה must be for this owner and not for another person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'for him', meaning for him and not for his fellow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the same פסוק. The word 'עליו' ('for him') shows that the offering must be done for its real owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of כפרה already gave us the rule about the type of offering. Now one word in it, 'עליו', gives us the rule about the owner: the atonement is for him only.

keyTerms.meaning: For him (the owner)
His fellow, another person

phrases.english: The verse says: "for him"
for him, and not for his fellow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא עָלָיו עָלָיו וְלֹא עַל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 from the same פסוק used in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עליו' teaches that the עבודה must be for the real owner and not for another.

steps.title: Is this rule required or only the ideal way?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוקים show that doing it לשמה is a מצוה. Where do we see that it is לעכב, meaning the קרבן is פסול without it?
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found that it is a מצוה. From where do we know that it is indispensable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether these rules are just the proper way to do it, or whether breaking them actually disqualifies the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק can teach how something should be done without saying that it fails if done another way. The גמרא needs extra proof that doing it שלא לשמה makes a חטאת פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: As a מצוה, the proper way to do it from the start
Indispensable: without it, the act is invalid

steps.confusionAlert: 'למצוה' does not mean 'not important'. It means 'this is how you should do it', but if you did it differently, it still counts. 'לעכב' means that if you did it differently, it does not count at all.

phrases.english: We have found it as a מצוה;
that it is indispensable, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how strong the rules found in steps 1 to 5 really are.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that doing it שלא לשמה actually disqualifies the חטאת.

steps.title: 'His sin offering' shows it is required
steps.stepSummary: Using the method of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: the Torah could have said 'חטאת' but said 'חטאתו', and this extra wording shows that the rule is לעכב.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: 'sin offering' versus 'his sin offering'. Here too: 'sin offering' versus 'his sin offering'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a reasoning that רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע used elsewhere: the word 'his' is extra, and an extra word like this makes the rule required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain word 'חטאת' would have been enough to say what the קרבן is. The Torah wrote 'מחטאתו', with 'his' added, and this extra emphasis on the owner turns the rule into a requirement. So a חטאת not sprinkled for its owner is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: As (so-and-so) said
His sin offering
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: A חטאת whose blood is sprinkled for a different owner is פסול. The extra word 'his' (חטאתו) shows that this rule about the owner is לעכב and not just למצוה. For a change of offering type, so far we only have a מצוה; the next step points this out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first source showing that doing a חטאת for the wrong owner can actually disqualify it. That makes the חטאת different from most other קרבנות, which still count even when done שלא לשמה.

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: As Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
"sin offering" versus "his sin offering";
phrases.notes: The Torah could have just said חטאת, but it said חטאתו. That extra 'his' makes it a must.

phrases.english: here too: "sin offering" versus "his sin offering."
phrases.notes: Here the word is מחטאתו, from the פסוק of כפרה in ויקרא 4:26.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ חַטָּאת חַטָּאתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by bringing in a known method of reading the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'his' in 'מחטאתו' shows that doing it לשמה is לעכב.

steps.title: What about all the other rites?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists what has been proven so far and asks for a source that covers all the עבודות, not just the זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found that it is a מצוה not to change the type of offering, and that for the sprinkling a change of owner matters both as a מצוה and לעכב. But where do we learn that in all the rites a change of offering type makes it פסול, and that in the other rites a change of owner matters both as a מצוה and לעכב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up what earlier steps proved and points out what is still missing. It sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a change of offering type, the sources so far only show a מצוה, not that it disqualifies. For a change of owner, they come from the כפרה פסוק, so they only cover the זריקה. So we still need a source that שינוי קודש is לעכב in every עבודה, and that שינוי בעלים matters (מצוה and לעכב) in the other עבודות.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for)
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
The sacrificial rites (שחיטה, קבלה, הולכה, זריקה)
The rest, the other ones
From where do we learn it?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is doubting the earlier proofs. It accepts them and only says they cover the זריקה, not the other עבודות.

phrases.english: We have found the מצוה regarding a change of offering type,
and for the sprinkling, regarding a change of owner,
both as a מצוה and as indispensable.
phrases.notes: This sums up Steps 3 through 7, which all came from the פסוק about כפרה, and כפרה happens through the sprinkling.

phrases.english: That it is indispensable in all the rites regarding a change of offering type,
and in the other rites regarding a change of owner,
both as a מצוה and as indispensable, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 7 by pointing out that the proofs so far only covered the זריקה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that all עבודות must be done without שינוי קודש (לעכב), and the other עבודות without שינוי בעלים (מצוה and לעכב).

steps.title: רבי יונה learns it from the נזיר's sin offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה brings the פסוק about the חטאת of a נזיר. The word 'ועשה' teaches that every action must be done לשם חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונה said: we learn it from the חטאת of a נזיר. The פסוק says 'the כהן shall bring them before ה׳ and shall do his חטאת and his עולה.' This teaches that all of its actions must be done for the sake of a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונה answers the question with a new פסוק. 'Doing' the חטאת includes every action, not just the sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier פסוק spoke about כפרה, so it only covered the זריקה. This פסוק uses the general word 'ועשה' (and he shall do), which covers all the עבודות. That gives us the rule for שינוי קודש in every עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from, it is learned from
The חטאת a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות
All of its actions or doings

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the rule of לשמה for a חטאת cover every stage of the קרבן, not only the sprinkling of the blood.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yona said:
It is learned from the sin offering of a nazir,
as it is written: "And the kohen shall bring them before ה׳
and shall do his sin offering and his burnt offering"
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:16

phrases.english: that all of its actions must be for the sake of a sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה: אָתְיָא מֵחַטַּאת נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק of the נזיר's חטאת, 'ועשה את חטאתו', teaches that every action must be לשם חטאת.

steps.title: What about a change of owner in the other rites?
steps.stepSummary: The new source covers a change of offering type. The גמרא asks where we learn that a change of owner is also a problem in the other עבודות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for a change of offering type. Where do we learn the rule for a change of owner? (The printed text continues here, though some versions leave these words out: if the פסוק is not needed for a change of type, apply it to a change of owner. We found it as a מצוה; where do we learn it is לעכב?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבי יונה's source for שינוי קודש. It now asks for the matching source for שינוי בעלים, which sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לשם חטאת' is about the type of קרבן, not about who owns it. So we still need something in the פסוק that points to the owner. The bracketed lines suggest an extra line of reasoning that some versions leave out.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this topic
Apply it to another topic

phrases.english: We have found a change of offering type;
a change of owner, from where do we know?
(If it is not needed for a change of offering type,
phrases.notes: These words in round brackets appear in the printed גמרא, but some versions leave them out.

phrases.english: apply it to a change of owner.
We have found it as a מצוה; that it is indispensable, from where do we know?)

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן שִׁנּוּי קֹדֶשׁ, שִׁנּוּי בְּעָלִים מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on Step 9's answer, the same way Step 4 followed up on Step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a change of owner in the other עבודות also makes the חטאת פסול.

steps.title: The extra word 'his'
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the פסוק could have said 'חטאת' but says 'חטאתו', and that points to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: the Torah could have said 'חטאת' but said 'חטאתו', his sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע uses the same method as in Step 7. Here he applies it to the נזיר's פסוק, so it covers all the עבודות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending 'ו' ('his') ties the קרבן to its owner, so it must be done for him. Because the word is extra, it shows the rule is לעכב, so changing the owner in any עבודה makes the קרבן פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: His sin offering (the extra 'his' points to the owner)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יונה and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, every עבודה of a חטאת must be done for a חטאת (from 'ועשה') and for its owner (from 'חטאתו'), and both rules are לעכב. רבינא and the גמרא challenge this proof in the next steps, and רבא brings a different source.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
"Sin offering" versus "his sin offering."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: חַטָּאת חַטָּאתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 using the same reading method as Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'his' in 'חטאתו' in the נזיר's פסוק teaches that every עבודה must be for the owner, and that this is לעכב.

steps.title: רבינא asks: what would 'His Burnt Offering' teach?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא attacks the 'חטאתו' derivation. The same פסוק says 'עולתו', so if the extra 'ו' teaches something for the חטאת, what would it teach for the עולה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objects: If that is true, then the פסוק also could have said 'עולת' but said 'עולתו'. What do you learn from that?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the last answer. If the extra 'ו' in 'חטאתו' teaches a rule, then the extra 'ו' in 'עולתו' in the same פסוק should teach a rule too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in Step 11 depends on reading the extra 'ו' as a lesson about the owner. But the same פסוק also says 'ואת עולתו', and nobody learns from that 'ו' that an עולה brought for the wrong owner is disqualified. So maybe the 'ו' is just normal wording and teaches nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it. This introduces a strong challenge.
If that is so. It takes your logic and pushes it further to show a problem.
A burnt offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח.
What do you learn from it?

phrases.english: Ravina objects to this:
If that is so,
"burnt offering" – "his burnt offering"
phrases.notes: The same פסוק about the נזיר says 'ואת עולתו' right next to 'חטאתו' (במדבר 6:16).

phrases.english: what do you learn from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the derivation from 'חטאתו' given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's reading of the extra 'ו' in 'חטאתו' as a lesson about the owner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same extra 'ו' appears in 'עולתו' in the same פסוק and teaches nothing there, so the 'ו' in 'חטאתו' may also teach nothing.

steps.title: Why didn't רבינא also ask about 'His Meal Offering' and 'His Libation'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבינא picked only 'עולתו'. The next פסוק also says 'מנחתו' and 'נסכו' with the same extra 'ו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבינא, the פסוק also says 'מנחתו' instead of 'מנחת' and 'נסכו' instead of 'נסך'. What do you learn from those?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks רבינא's question. If he wanted examples of an extra 'ו', there are more of them nearby, so why did he mention only the עולה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two more words in the same section have the extra 'ו': 'מנחתו' and 'נסכו'. If those also teach nothing, רבינא could have used them for his challenge. The גמרא wants to know why he left them out.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering made of flour.
A libation, wine poured on the מזבח.
And according to רבינא

phrases.english: And according to Ravina,
"meal offering" – "his meal offering",
"libation" – "his libation",
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:17.

phrases.english: what do you learn from them?
phrases.notes: The question is why רבינא didn't use these words for his challenge too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines how רבינא built his challenge in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבינא challenged only from 'עולתו' and not also from 'מנחתו' and 'נסכו'.

steps.title: 'His Meal Offering' and 'His Libation' teach something else
steps.stepSummary: The extra wording of 'מנחתו' and 'נסכו' is needed for its own lesson. Like 'מנחתם ונסכיהם', it teaches that these can be brought at night and even the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: That wording is needed: it is like 'מנחתם ונסכיהם', which teaches that they can be brought at night, and even the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבינא could not use 'מנחתו' and 'נסכו', because those words already teach a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like 'מנחתם ונסכיהם' in the קרבנות of the holidays, the possessive form shows that the מנחה and נסכים belong to the קרבן but can be brought later. They can be brought at night or on the next day. So the 'ו' in those words is used up, and only 'עולתו' is left as a real problem.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for a different lesson.
Their meal offering and their libations. This phrase appears in the קרבנות of the holidays.
At night
On the next day

phrases.english: That is needed:
"their meal offering and their libations" – even at night,
phrases.notes: For example במדבר 29:37.

phrases.english: "their meal offering and their libations" – even the next day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מנחתו' and 'נסכו' are needed to teach that the מנחה and נסכים may be brought at night and even the next day, so רבינא could not challenge from them.

steps.title: The question on 'His Burnt Offering' still stands
steps.stepSummary: After explaining 'מנחתו' and 'נסכו', the גמרא goes back to רבינא's challenge. 'עולתו' still has no lesson, so the 'חטאתו' proof is still in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But 'עולת' changed to 'עולתו': what do you learn from that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבינא's original challenge and says it has not been answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side question about מנחה and נסכים is settled, but it did not help the 'חטאתו' proof. The extra 'ו' in 'עולתו' still seems to teach nothing. That keeps the doubt on whether the 'ו' in 'חטאתו' teaches anything.

keyTerms.meaning: His burnt offering
But, meaning the question still stands
From them

phrases.english: But "burnt offering" – "his burnt offering",
what do you learn from them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבינא's challenge from Step 12 after the side issue in Steps 13-14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra 'ו' in 'עולתו' still has no lesson, so the matching 'ו' in 'חטאתו' may not teach anything either.

steps.title: Can the two kinds of חטאת be learned from each other?
steps.stepSummary: A second problem: an ordinary חטאת (like one for eating forbidden fat) and the חטאת of a נזיר each have a special stricter feature. So maybe rules cannot be carried from one to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, can they be learned from each other? A חטאת for forbidden fat cannot be learned from a נזיר's חטאת, since the נזיר's has other blood with it. A נזיר's חטאת cannot be learned from a חטאת for fat, since that one comes for a sin punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new, separate problem with how the sources were combined. It asks whether a rule written about one kind of חטאת can be applied to the other kind at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof so far mixed sources about an ordinary חטאת with a source about the חטאת of a נזיר (Step 9). The ordinary חטאת cannot learn from the נזיר's, because the נזיר brings other קרבנות together with his. The נזיר's cannot learn from the ordinary one, because the ordinary one atones for a sin punished with כרת. Each has a feature that might explain a stricter rule, so the comparison could break down in both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore. This brings an extra challenge.
Learn from each other
A חטאת brought for eating forbidden fat by mistake
The חטאת a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות
Other blood, meaning other קרבנות brought along with it
Being cut off. This is the heavenly punishment for doing the sin on purpose.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רבינא's question. This is a separate attack. Even if every word in the פסוק teaches something, the two kinds of חטאת might still be too different to learn from each other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of learning from a comparison. If each case has its own stricter feature, a rule found in one cannot simply be carried over to the other.

phrases.english: And furthermore, can they be learned from each other?!

phrases.aramaic: חַטַּאת חֵלֶב מֵחַטַּאת נָזִיר לָא גָּמְרָה –
phrases.english: A sin offering for forbidden fat cannot be learned from a nazirite's sin offering –
since there is other blood with it;
phrases.notes: The נזיר also brings an עולה and a שלמים, so his חטאת never comes alone.

phrases.aramaic: חַטַּאת נָזִיר מֵחַטַּאת חֵלֶב לָא גָּמְרָה –
phrases.english: A nazirite's sin offering cannot be learned from a sin offering for fat –
since it involves karet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate attack on top of רבינא's challenge, this time on combining sources from two different kinds of חטאת.
steps.kashyaTarget: Combining sources about an ordinary חטאת with sources about a נזיר's חטאת to build one rule for all עבודות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each kind of חטאת has its own stricter feature: other blood for the נזיר, and כרת for the ordinary חטאת. So neither can be the source for the other.

steps.title: רבא's new source: the leper's sin offering
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops the earlier proofs and learns the rule from the חטאת of a מצורע, where the פסוק says 'and the כהן shall make the חטאת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: we learn it from the חטאת of a מצורע. The פסוק says 'And the כהן shall make the חטאת', which teaches that every action done with it must be for the sake of a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier proofs were knocked down, רבא offers a brand-new source: the חטאת of a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וְעָשָׂה' (and he shall make) is read as covering all the 'making' actions of the קרבן. So every עבודה must be done לשם חטאת, and if it is not, the קרבן is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous idea and starts fresh)
The sin offering brought by a מצורע when he becomes pure
Its actions, all the עבודות done with the קרבן
For the sake of a sin offering

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is learned from the sin offering of a leper,
as it is written: "And the priest shall make the sin offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:19

phrases.english: meaning that all its actions must be for the sake of a sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אָתְיָא מֵחַטַּאת מְצוֹרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'חטאתו' and נזיר proofs were challenged, רבא replaces them with a new source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source replaces the challenged derivations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule had to come from 'חטאתו' or from the נזיר's חטאת, which were both shaky.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule comes from 'וְעָשָׂה הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַחַטָּאת' by the מצורע: all actions must be לשם חטאת.

steps.title: What about changing the owner?
steps.stepSummary: The new פסוק covers changing the type of קרבן. The גמרא asks where we learn that changing the owner also makes it פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for changing the type of קרבן. Where do we learn the rule for changing the owner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבא's source for one kind of wrong intent and asks for a source for the second kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to do a קרבן 'not for its sake': thinking of it as a different קרבן (שינוי קודש) or as someone else's קרבן (שינוי בעלים). 'וְעָשָׂה אֶת הַחַטָּאת' only speaks about the type of קרבן, so the owner needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: Changing the type of קרבן in one's intent, like thinking of a חטאת as an עולה
Changing the owner in one's intent, doing it for someone else
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And we have found a source for changing the type of offering;
changing the owner, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַשְׁכְּחַן שִׁנּוּי קֹדֶשׁ, שִׁנּוּי בְּעָלִים מְנָלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבא's source and asks about the second kind of שלא לשמה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a חטאת done for the wrong owner is פסול.

steps.title: The source for the owner: 'for the one being purified'
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק says 'וְכִפֶּר עַל הַמִּטַּהֵר', teaching that the קרבן must be for this person, not for another.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'And he shall atone for the one being purified'. That means for this person being purified, and not for another person being purified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עַל הַמִּטַּהֵר' is read as 'this particular person'. So if the כהן does it for a different מצורע, it is a change of owner, and the קרבן is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall atone
The one being purified (the מצורע)
His fellow, another person

phrases.english: The verse states: "And he shall atone for the one being purified, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:19, the same פסוק as before.

phrases.english: for this one being purified,
and not for his fellow who is being purified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עַל הַמִּטַּהֵר' means this person only, so changing the owner makes it פסול.
steps.whatToRemember: By the מצורע: 'וְעָשָׂה אֶת הַחַטָּאת' covers changing the type of קרבן, and 'עַל הַמִּטַּהֵר' covers changing the owner.

steps.title: A leper's sin offering and an ordinary one cannot teach each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: an ordinary חטאת (for eating forbidden fat) and a מצורע's חטאת each have a special feature, so neither can teach the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, can they be learned from each other? A חטאת for eating forbidden fat cannot be learned from a מצורע's חטאת, because the מצורע brings other קרבנות with it. And a מצורע's חטאת cannot be learned from a חטאת for forbidden fat, because that one comes for a sin punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's proof in the same way it attacked the נזיר proof: the two kinds of חטאת are too different to learn from one another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע's חטאת is special because other blood (an עולה and an אשם) comes with it, so maybe only it is extra strict. An ordinary חטאת is special because it atones for a sin with כרת, so maybe only it is strict. Each has its own reason to be strict, so we cannot carry the rule across in either direction.

keyTerms.meaning: But still (a problem is still left)
From each other
The ordinary חטאת, for eating forbidden fat by mistake
Other blood, meaning other קרבנות brought together with it
Being cut off, a heavenly punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is asking to learn the מצורע from itself. The question is whether the ordinary חטאת can learn its rule from the מצורע's חטאת, since רבא's פסוק is written by the מצורע.

phrases.english: But still, can they be learned from each other?!

phrases.aramaic: חַטַּאת חֵלֶב מֵחַטַּאת מְצוֹרָע לָא יָלְפָא –
phrases.english: A sin offering for forbidden fat cannot be learned from a leper's sin offering,
since there is other blood with it;
phrases.notes: The מצורע also brings an עולה and an אשם along with his חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: חַטָּאת מְצוֹרָע מֵחַטַּאת חֵלֶב לָא גָּמְרָה –
phrases.english: a leper's sin offering cannot be learned from a sin offering for forbidden fat,
since that one is for a sin of karet!
phrases.notes: Eating forbidden fat on purpose is punished with כרת, which makes its חטאת more serious.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's source with the same kind of attack used on the נזיר proof in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's learning of the ordinary חטאת's rule from the מצורע's חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each kind has a unique strict feature (other blood with it / כרת), so the rule might belong only to that kind and cannot be carried across.

steps.title: Learning one from two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: one kind cannot teach another alone, but two kinds together can teach the third.
steps.simpleTranslation: It cannot come from one, but one can come from two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rescues the proof by combining sources: two kinds of חטאת together teach the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each single kind has a special feature that blocks learning from it alone. But when two different kinds both have the rule, the special feature of one is not shared by the other, so the rule is not because of those features. Then the rule can be carried to the third kind.

keyTerms.meaning: From one (source)
Let it come, let it be learned
From two (sources)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא answers 'each case has its own strictness': combine two different cases so that their special features cancel out.

phrases.english: From one it cannot come,
phrases.notes: The three kinds of חטאת here are: the ordinary one for forbidden fat, the נזיר's, and the מצורע's.

phrases.english: let one come from two.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵחֲדָא לָא אָתְיָא, תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20 (and the similar one in step 16).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining two sources to teach a third
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since each kind of חטאת has its own strict feature, no kind can teach another.
steps.terutzMaskana: One kind alone cannot teach, but two kinds together can teach the third, since their different special features cannot explain the shared rule.
steps.whatToRemember: Each kind of חטאת has something special, so one cannot teach another alone. The גמרא proposes that two together teach the third, and steps 22 to 24 test this and reject it.

steps.title: Which of the three is the extra one? Not the חטאת חלב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the three חטאות the Torah could have left out. It tries leaving out the חטאת חלב, but the other two (נזיר and מצורע) come with other קרבנות' blood, so they cannot teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one should the Torah not have written? Should it not write it about the חטאת for eating forbidden fat, and we learn it from the other two? But those two are special, because other blood comes along with them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the idea from the last step: if two kinds can teach the third, which one is the 'third' that needs no פסוק? This is the first try, and it fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To use 'two teach the third', one of the three cases must have no special feature that the other two share. The חטאת of a נזיר and of a מצורע both come together with other קרבנות (other blood), but the חטאת חלב comes alone. So the rule might apply only to a חטאת that comes with other blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one should the Torah not have written? (which case is extra)
And let it be learned from those (other cases)
What about those? (they are special, so they cannot teach)
The חטאת brought for eating forbidden fat by mistake (the ordinary חטאת)
Other blood: other קרבנות brought along with this one

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question from scratch. The גמרא is checking whether its own answer from the last step (two teach the third) actually works.

phrases.english: Regarding which one should the Torah not have written it?
Let the Merciful One not write it regarding the חטאת for forbidden fat,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. They just repeat 'let the Torah not write it.'

phrases.english: and let it be learned from those others?!
What about those others?
They are special, since other blood comes with them!
phrases.notes: A נזיר and a מצורע bring other קרבנות together with their חטאת; the חטאת חלב comes by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'two teach the third' answer of step 21 by testing the first possible pair.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חטאת נזיר and חטאת מצורע together can teach חטאת חלב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both teaching cases share a feature (other blood comes with them) that the learned case lacks, so the rule may depend on that feature.

steps.title: Not the חטאת of a נזיר either
steps.stepSummary: Trying to leave out the חטאת נזיר and learn it from מצורע and חלב also fails, because those two cannot be cancelled by asking a חכם, while a נזיר's vow can be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should the Torah not write it about the חטאת of a נזיר, and we learn it from the other two? But those two are special, since they cannot be undone by asking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second pair: learn the נזיר from the מצורע and the חטאת חלב. This try also fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר can go to a חכם and have his vow released, which cancels his need to bring the חטאת at all. A מצורע and a person who ate חלב have no such way out. So the rule might apply only to a חטאת that can never be cancelled, and it could not be extended to a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The חטאת a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות
Asking a חכם to release a vow, which cancels it

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write it regarding the חטאת of a נזיר,
and let it be learned from those others?!
What about those others?
They are special, since they cannot be undone by asking!
phrases.notes: A נזיר can ask a חכם to release his vow and then owes no קרבן; the other two can't get out of theirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second possible pair after the first one failed in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חטאת מצורע and חטאת חלב together can teach חטאת נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both teaching cases share a feature (no release by asking a חכם) that the נזיר lacks.

steps.title: Not the חטאת of a מצורע either
steps.stepSummary: Trying to leave out the חטאת מצורע and learn it from נזיר and חלב fails too, because those two never change for a poor person, while a poor מצורע brings a bird instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should the Torah not write it about the חטאת of a מצורע, and we learn it from the other two? But those two are special, since they are never brought in a cheaper form for a poor person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last pair: learn the מצורע from the נזיר and the חטאת חלב. This fails as well, so no pair works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor מצורע may bring a cheaper קרבן (birds) instead of an animal, but the חטאת of a נזיר and the חטאת חלב have no such option. So the rule might apply only to a חטאת that is the same for rich and poor. Now all three pairs have failed, and 'two teach the third' cannot work here.

keyTerms.meaning: The חטאת brought by a מצורע when he becomes טהור
Brought in a poor form: a cheaper קרבן for someone who cannot afford the usual one

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three חטאות has something special about it, so no two of them together can teach the third. The 'two teach the third' method fails here.

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write it regarding the חטאת of a מצורע,
and let it be learned from those others?!
What about those others?
They are special, since they do not come in a poor person's form!
phrases.notes: A poor מצורע brings birds instead of a sheep (ויקרא 14:21); the other two always stay the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the test of all three pairs, showing the step 21 method fails entirely.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that חטאת נזיר and חטאת חלב together can teach חטאת מצורע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both teaching cases share a feature (never brought in a poor form) that the מצורע lacks.

steps.title: The rule comes from comparing חטאת to שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the 'two teach the third' approach and uses a היקש: the פסוק lists חטאת together with שלמים, so just as שלמים must be brought for their own sake in both type and owner, so must every חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק says: 'This is the law of the עולה and of the מנחה, and so on.' The פסוק compares חטאת to שלמים. Just as with שלמים we need it to be brought for its own sake as the proper way, whether the change is in the type of קרבן or in the owner, so too with חטאת we need it for its own sake, both in type and in owner.
steps.whatsHappening: Since no pair of חטאות can teach the third, the גמרא brings a brand new source: a פסוק that puts all the קרבנות in one list. This supplies the מצוה part of the answer; the next step explains that the לעכב comes from the separate פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that the earlier method is dropped. ויקרא ז:לז lists חטאת and שלמים in the same sentence, and that joining (a היקש) means rules of שלמים carry over to חטאת. Because the היקש is a general comparison, it covers every kind of חטאת, and it covers both a change of קרבן type and a change of owner.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק compared it: placed two things together so one's rules apply to the other (a הֶקֵּשׁ)
Peace offerings
Changing the type of קרבן in one's intent (thinking of it as a different קרבן)
Changing the owner in one's intent (bringing it for a different person)
For its own sake, as the proper way to do the מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: The source that every חטאת should be brought לשמה as a מצוה, both in type of קרבן and in owner, is the היקש of חטאת to שלמים in ויקרא ז:לז. The next step shows that the 'must' (לעכב) comes from the separate פסוקים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This one היקש solves the problem the three separate חטאות could not: it reaches all חטאות at once and covers both kinds of wrong intent.

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says:
"This is the law of the burnt offering and of the meal offering, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:37. The 'etc.' continues the list: חטאת, אשם, מילואים, and שלמים.

phrases.english: The verse compared it to peace offerings;
just as with peace offerings,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שִׁנּוּי קֹדֶשׁ בֵּין שִׁנּוּי בְּעָלִים,
phrases.english: whether a change of offering type or a change of owner,
we require it to be for its own sake, as the מצוה;
so too a sin offering,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שִׁנּוּי קֹדֶשׁ בֵּין שִׁנּוּי בְּעָלִים,
phrases.english: whether a change of offering type or a change of owner,
we require it to be for its own sake, as the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed 'two teach the third' method (steps 21 to 24) with a new source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source (היקש) replacing the rejected derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the rule could be built from the three special חטאות, two teaching the third.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each חטאת is special, so the rule comes instead from the היקש of חטאת to שלמים, covering both change of type and change of owner for all חטאות.

steps.title: The basic rule comes from שלמים, and the extra verses make it a must
steps.stepSummary: The מצוה of לשמה for every חטאת comes from the היקש to שלמים. The separate פסוקים for each חטאת teach that it is לעכב, meaning the קרבן is invalid without it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the basic requirement is learned from שלמים, and those other verses are there to teach that it is essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its answer. The basic rule comes from שלמים, and the three separate פסוקים are not wasted, because they teach that the rule is essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A היקש to שלמים can only teach that לשמה is a מצוה, because שלמים brought for the wrong purpose still count. So the separate פסוקים written for each kind of חטאת add something new: for that kind, the wrong intention makes the קרבן פסול. Since each kind has its own פסוק for לעכב, there is no need to learn one kind from another, so the objections of steps 16 to 24 no longer matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore, so
The ideal way to do it from the start (if not done, it may still count)
To hold back. The rule is essential, and without it the קרבן is invalid
Verses (פסוקים)

steps.whatToRemember: For a חטאת, לשמה is not just a nice extra. The שלמים comparison teaches the מצוה, and the separate פסוקים teach that it is לעכב, so a חטאת brought שלא לשמה is פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the היקש to שלמים alone makes a חטאת שלא לשמה פסול. שלמים brought שלא לשמה are still kosher, so the היקש only gives the מצוה. The 'must' comes from the extra פסוקים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the משנה's rule that a חטאת brought שלא לשמה is פסול, unlike most קרבנות. It also shows why every one of the three פסוקים is needed.

phrases.english: Therefore, the basic requirement comes from שלמים,
phrases.notes: This is the היקש from step 25: just as שלמים are brought לשמה, so is every חטאת.

phrases.english: and those verses are to make it essential.
phrases.notes: These are the separate פסוקים written for חטאת חלב, נזיר and מצורע.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִילְכָּךְ, מִצְוָה – מִשְּׁלָמִים, וְהָנָךְ קְרָאֵי – לְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the היקש answer from step 25 by giving a job to the three separate פסוקים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: לשמה for every חטאת is a מצוה learned from שלמים, and the specific פסוקים make it לעכב.

steps.title: Listing the sources found so far, starting with the חטאת for חלב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to review which חטאות have a clear source. The חטאת for eating חלב has one, because the פסוק says 'לחטאת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for the חטאת brought for eating חלב, since the תורה writes 'for a חטאת' about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question. It starts by listing a case that already has a clear source, so it can then ask about the cases that don't.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ואשכחן' means 'we have found,' and the גמרא uses it to list what is already settled before pointing out a gap. The word 'לחטאת' in the פסוק of חטאת חלב shows it must be slaughtered for the sake of a חטאת. This prepares the question about the other kinds of חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: And we have found (a source for)
The חטאת brought for accidentally eating forbidden fat
For a חטאת, meaning for the sake of a חטאת

phrases.english: And we have found a source for the חטאת for forbidden fat,
since it is written about it: 'for a חטאת';
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:33

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַשְׁכְּחַן חַטַּאת חֵלֶב, דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ לַחַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 26: if each kind of חטאת needs its own פסוק to make לשמה לעכב, the גמרא now lists which kinds have such a פסוק, starting with חטאת חלב, before asking about the rest.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Setting up a question: we have sources for some חטאות, but what about the others?
